info.title: LiveCert — Sourced Answers for Agents
info.description: Sourced answers for agents and apps across 36 intents, each read live from a named primary source so the caller can check it. Every answer opens with a one-sentence answer, then returns the values as fields, the source and the time it was checked. Compliance: sanctions screening of people, companies and wallets against the OFAC SDN and UN lists with near-match scores; company register records (status, company number, register, registered address and agent, parents) from GLEIF and SEC EDGAR; SEC filings with acceptance times and each 10-Q or 10-K's own XBRL figures; URL reputation from Cloudflare and Quad9 threat DNS and URLhaus, each source named. Research: question answering with every claim cited, web search with dated reports, fact checks with the source URL and evidence sentence, and academic, clinical and news search. Markets: prices and market data for coins, tokens and listed companies, 10-K revenue and earnings, exchange rates and macroeconomic prints (US CPI and unemployment from BLS, the federal funds target range from the New York Fed, euro-area HICP from Eurostat and ECB rates). On-chain: transfer verification with confirmations and the burned base fee, transaction and contract activity across EVM chains, wallet balances, gas, token holders and cross-chain messages. Security: live TLS certificates, URL scans, CVE records and fraud signals. Weather: forecasts, current conditions and storm risk. Also translation, IP geolocation, prediction market outcomes, text extraction, sentiment and classification. Only the question-answering, sentiment and classification sentences are phrased by a model, each with a keyless fallback, and a phrased answer is kept only when every claim cites a numbered source; everything else is computed, not generated.

get.description: Example questions: "Is the TLS certificate for github.com valid?", "When does example.com's certificate expire?". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and domain, valid, chain_complete, issuer, valid_to, days_remaining. Live TLS certificate check for one domain. Accepts a bare hostname, a full URL, or host:port.

parameters.description: Hostname to check. Accepts example.com, https://example.com/path, or example.com:8443.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The user's original question, verbatim. The hostname is extracted from it.

200.description: Always 200: an answer, or confidence 0 with an error code. Never a made-up value.

Accepts a place name or "lat,lon".

get.description: Example questions: "What is the ETH balance of vitalik.eth?", "Balance of 0x… on Base". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and address, chain, balance_eth, symbol. Native-coin balance of an EVM address, read with eth_getBalance at the latest block from public JSON-RPC on the chain the question names — Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism or Polygon. A zero balance is reported as zero; an RPC that does not answer is reported as unavailable rather than as zero. Token balances such as USDT are not included, and the answer says so when one was asked about.

parameters.description: The 20-byte EVM address to read, e.g. 0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc454e4438f44e.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The user's original question, verbatim. It names the chain and any token asked about alongside the native coin.

200.description: Always 200: an answer, or confidence 0 with an error code. Never a made-up value.

get.description: On-chain activity, asked about a transaction or about an address. Example questions: "Did transaction 0x… succeed, and who sent it to whom?", "When was contract 0x… deployed and how many transactions does it have?". For a transaction it returns verdict and a transaction object with status, from, to, value_wei, value, symbol, block_number, block_hash, receipt_status, method, gas_used, fee_wei, confirmations, base_fee_wei and base_fee_burned, which is true on Ethereum and Polygon, where the EIP-1559 base fee is burned, and false on rollups, where it is paid to the sequencer. A transaction is read by hash from public JSON-RPC on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, BNB Chain or Avalanche; where no chain is named every one of them is searched rather than one being assumed. It reports confirmed, reverted, pending or not found, with the sender and recipient, value moved, total fee, the base fee and whether it was burned, confirmations, gas used, block number, any contract deployed and the count of ERC-20 transfers in the receipt. An address is answered from the chain and its block explorer on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism or Polygon: whether it is a contract, an externally owned account, or an account carrying an EIP-7702 delegation; when a contract was deployed; how many transactions are recorded against it; how many an account has sent; and when it was last active, where a recency read the index could not date is reported as undated rather than as inactive. On Ethereum an explorer outage fails over to a second index whose count is attributed and may trail the chain. A reverted transaction is reported as reverted, not as a failure to answer; an RPC or explorer that does not respond is reported as unknown rather than as not found, because those are different facts; and a chain this endpoint does not read is named as unsupported rather than answered from a different chain.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: The 32-byte transaction hash, 0x followed by 64 hex characters. Omit it for a question about an address.

parameters.name: chain
parameters.description: One of ethereum, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, bsc or avalanche. When absent, a chain named in the question is used, and otherwise every chain is searched for a hash.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The user's original question, verbatim. A hash or an address, the chain, and what is asked about the address are read from it.

200.description: Always 200: an answer, or confidence 0 with an error code. Never a made-up value.

get.description: Example questions: "What is the severity and affected versions of CVE-2021-44228?". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and cve_id, severity, cvss_score, cvss_version, scored_by, affected_product, affected_versions, other_products_affected, cwe, status, published, description, source, source_url. Vulnerabilities from the National Vulnerability Database, asked three ways. By CVE identifier: the severity rating and CVSS base score with the CVSS version and the source that assigned it, the affected product and versions resolved from the record's CPE configuration — exact versions and half-open ranges alike — and what the flaw is. By year or severity, such as "critical CVEs 2025" or "latest CVEs": the vulnerabilities published in a stated window of at most 120 days with the highest-scored named, where a severity band is applied to each record's own CVSS base score rather than to the database's severity flag. By product and vulnerability class, such as "Forgejo remote code execution": the matching record and the fixed release where one is documented, used only when the record names the product asked about. A record with no CVSS score yet is reported as unscored rather than given an invented severity; a REJECTED identifier is reported as rejected rather than as not found; a truncated identifier is named as incomplete; and a rate-limited or unreachable database is reported as unknown, never as a vulnerability that does not exist.

parameters.name: cve_id
parameters.description: The CVE identifier, e.g. CVE-2024-3094. Omit it for a question by year, severity or product.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The user's original question, verbatim. An identifier, a year, a severity such as critical, or a product and vulnerability class are read from it.

200.description: Always 200: an answer, or confidence 0 with an error code. Never a made-up value.

get.description: Example questions: "Latest news about the EU AI Act", "What happened with Boeing this week?". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and subject, window_days, articles, count. News article coverage of a topic, entity or time period, searched rather than browsed. Returns individual articles — each with its headline, the publisher that ran it and its publication date, most relevant first — for a subject read from the question, over a window the question may state ("in the last 3 days", "this month"). A recency word with no explicit window is treated as a request rather than a filter: the last 30 days are searched first and the search is widened only if nothing on the subject was published in them, and the answer says when that happened. Articles that are not about the subject are dropped rather than used as padding, with the acronym of a named entity counted as naming it. This is article coverage; a plain list of current headlines is /headlines. A news index that does not respond is reported as unknown, never as an absence of coverage.

parameters.name: topic
parameters.description: The subject to search for: a topic, company, person or event. Read from the question when absent.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Only return articles published within this many days. Read from the question when absent; omitted means no date restriction.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The user's original question, verbatim. The subject and the time window are read from it.

200.description: Always 200: an answer, or confidence 0 with an error code. Never a made-up value.

get.description: Example questions: "Convert 100 USD to EUR", "What is 5,000 yen in dollars?". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and from, to, amount, rate, converted, kind, as_of. An exchange rate, or an amount converted between two currencies. The primary source is the European Central Bank's euro foreign exchange reference rate, which is published once per day and therefore does not move between reads; the answer states that it is a reference rate and the date it was published for, so it is never mistaken for a live trading quote. The rate is given in both directions and the conversion direction is taken from the question, including the "how many X is Y" phrasing that names the target first. Currencies the ECB does not publish fall back to a market rate, and that answer says it is a market rate instead. A request naming only one currency is refused rather than half-answered, and a source that does not respond is reported as unknown rather than as a rate of zero.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: ISO 4217 code of the currency being converted from, e.g. USD. Read from the question when absent.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: ISO 4217 code of the currency being converted to, e.g. EUR. Read from the question when absent.

parameters.name: amount
parameters.description: Amount to convert. Omitted means the question asks for the rate itself, and no amount is invented.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The user's original question, verbatim. Both currencies, the direction and the amount are read from it.

200.description: Always 200: an answer, or confidence 0 with an error code. Never a made-up value.

get.description: Example questions: "What is the gas price on Ethereum right now?", "Gas on Base in Gwei". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and chain, gwei, base_fee_gwei, priority_gwei, block. The current transaction fee level on a named chain, read from that chain's own JSON-RPC. Reports the gas price in Gwei both exactly and rounded, the base fee and priority fee that make it up, the block the reading is from so the figure is checkable, and what a standard 21,000-gas transfer costs at that rate. This is the fee level and never the chain token's price, which is a different intent. Covers ethereum, base, arbitrum, optimism and polygon; a chain outside that list is named as uncovered rather than answered with a different chain's fee, and an unresponsive endpoint is reported as unknown rather than as a fee of zero.

get.description: Example questions: "What is Solana's market cap and 24-hour volume?", "Apple's revenue and P/E from its 10-K". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and subject, name, chain, data. Market data and financial statistics for a coin, a token or a listed company, deliberately beyond a single quoted price. A coin named in words, such as Solana or Bitcoin, returns market capitalisation, 24-hour trading volume in dollars, fully diluted valuation, 24-hour range and change. A token contract address with its chain returns market capitalisation, 24-hour trading volume, fully diluted valuation and last traded price. A ticker or company name returns the day range, share volume, 52-week range and change against the previous close, with the ticker resolved from the company name where only a name is given. Revenue, net income and earnings per share come from the company's latest 10-K, and a price-to-earnings ratio is computed from the last traded price and the 10-K's diluted earnings per share, with both inputs named. A figure that could not be retrieved, such as margins, is stated as not retrieved rather than substituted.

parameters.description: Token contract address, e.g. 0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913. Use with the chain named in the question.

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: Ticker symbol or company name, e.g. AAPL or Apple. Read from the question when absent.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The user's original question, verbatim. The subject and chain are read from it.

200.description: Always 200: an answer, or confidence 0 with an error code. Never a made-up value.

get.description: Example questions: "Is 0x… a scam address?", "This email asks me to pay an invoice in gift cards: is it fraud?". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and subject, evidence, not_checked, sanctioned, flagged_hosts, scam_markers. How likely a named address, link or message is to be fraudulent, assessed from checks that are actually performed and named in the answer: the OFAC sanctioned digital-currency address listing, Cloudflare's threat-intelligence resolver for any domain in the text, the address's own on-chain state (contract, externally owned account, or an account carrying an EIP-7702 delegation, with its transaction count and balance), and specific scam wording such as a request for a seed phrase, gift-card payment or changed banking details. A sanctions hit or a domain blocked as malware is reported as high risk. A clean result is reported as no indicators found among the checks performed, with the checks listed, and explicitly not as a statement that the subject is safe; a check that could not be completed is named as such rather than counted as clean. An academic paper named by title is checked against OpenAlex's retraction record, and a retraction is reported as high risk. No keyless source records misconduct findings, paper-mill membership or predatory-publisher status, so the answer names those three as not checked rather than implying a clean record, and a title that cannot be matched to one indexed work is reported as not found rather than matched loosely to a similar one.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Wallet address, URL, message text, or the title of an academic paper to assess. Read from the question when absent.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The user's original question, verbatim, including the message being asked about.

200.description: Always 200: an answer, or confidence 0 with an error code. Never a made-up value.

get.description: Example questions: "How many holders does USDC have on Ethereum?". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and symbol, name, address, chain, holders, top_holder_percent. How many distinct addresses hold a named ERC-20 token, read from the chain's own transfer index via Blockscout. The token may be given as a contract address or as a symbol together with its chain, and where no chain is named every supported chain is checked rather than one being assumed, because the same symbol carries different holder counts on different chains. The answer names the contract the figure came from so it is checkable. Where the question also asks about concentration, the share of supply held by the single largest holder is reported, and where that list does not return in time the answer says so rather than omitting it silently. This is a headcount of holders and never a balance, a price, a supply figure or pool liquidity, each of which is a different intent. An identifier that is not a token, such as a CVE number, is named as such rather than searched for. Where more than one token on a chain shares a symbol with no dominant one among them, a contract address is asked for instead of one being picked. Covers ethereum, base, arbitrum, optimism and polygon.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: ERC-20 contract address, e.g. 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913. Read from the question when absent.

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: Token symbol, e.g. USDC. Used when no contract address is given.

parameters.name: chain
parameters.description: Chain to read: ethereum, base, arbitrum, optimism or polygon. Every supported chain is checked when absent.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The user's original question, verbatim. Carries the chain, and whether holder concentration was also asked for.

200.description: Always 200: an answer, or confidence 0 with an error code. Never a made-up value.

get.description: Example questions: "What clinical trials are testing semaglutide for Alzheimer's?". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and subject, trials, citations. An answer to one research question, drawn from named sources: the ClinicalTrials.gov registry for trial phase, status and completion dates, Europe PMC for published literature, and Wikipedia for subjects that are neither. Every source is cited by identifier — the NCT number of a trial, the title, first author and year of a paper — so the answer can be checked rather than taken on trust, and a source is only cited when it actually names the subject asked about. Where the question asks about an outcome that has not been decided, such as whether a drug will be approved, the registered evidence to date is reported and the answer states plainly that no decision has been recorded; no outcome is predicted. Where neither index holds anything on the subject that is what the answer says, named as an absence in those indexes rather than as an absence of research. A request to combine findings across many sources into a synthesis is the RESEARCH_SYNTHESIS intent rather than this one.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The research question, verbatim. The subject and any named drug, trial or organisation are read from it.

parameters.name: topic
parameters.description: The subject to research, when it is available separately from the question.

200.description: Always 200: an answer, or confidence 0 with an error code. Never a made-up value.

get.description: Example questions: "What is the price of ETH?", "BTC price in EUR on 2025-01-01". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and asset, symbol, price, quote, price_at, source, aggregate_price. The current or historical price of one named cryptocurrency, as a single quoted figure with the venue that quoted it and the UTC time of the quote. The current price is the last Coinbase trade where Coinbase lists the pair, Kraken's last trade where it does not, and CoinGecko's cross-venue aggregate as a cross-check or fallback; the answer says it is a live quote that moves between reads. The quote currency follows the question (USD by default; EUR, GBP, JPY, INR and other major fiat, or BTC and ETH). A dollar stablecoin's answer also states its distance from the one-dollar peg. A date returns that UTC day's Coinbase open and close and CoinGecko's daily snapshot, labelled as historical. This is one price, never market capitalisation or volume, which is FINANCIAL_DATA, and never what an address holds, which is WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK. A fork or wrapped asset such as Bitcoin Cash, Ethereum Classic or Wrapped Bitcoin is priced as itself, never as the major whose name it contains, and a multi-word coin name is matched whole. Testnet assets are answered as having no market price, a future date is declined as a prediction, an asset name that matches no listed coin exactly is not substituted with a similar one, and a provider outage is reported as an outage rather than a missing price.

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: Asset name or ticker, e.g. ETH or Ethereum. Read from the question when absent.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The user's original question, verbatim. The asset, the quote currency and any date are read from it.

200.description: Always 200: an answer, or confidence 0 with an error code. Never a made-up value.

get.description: Example questions: "What is Apple's share price?", "TSLA closing price on 2026-09-01". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and ticker, name, price, currency, price_at, exchange, market_open, source. The current or historical share price of one listed equity, given as a ticker or a company name. Every answer states the exchange, the quote time in the exchange's own time zone, and whether the regular trading session is open right now; outside the session the figure is labelled as the last session price and never presented as a live quote. A company name is resolved to its ticker and accepted only when the listing carries every word of the name asked about, so an unlisted subsidiary is answered as not found rather than with a related company's price. A ticker is read only when it is written as one in capitals, and a currency code such as (USD) is never taken for a ticker. A question that does not ask about a share price, such as a weather question naming a city, is refused rather than priced. An ISO date returns that day's closing price, and a date with no session is said to have none. A question asking whether a stock will rise or fall is answered with the price and an explicit statement that no forecast is made. get.description: Example questions: "What is the sentiment of this review: 'The product broke after one day'?". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and compound, positive_words, negative_words, tones. The sentiment a supplied text expresses — positive, negative, neutral or mixed — read by a hosted open-weight language model called over the network, which writes the label and a short explanation. When that model does not answer within its time budget the text is read instead with a rule-based word list and the VADER method (negation, intensifiers, a contrastive "but", capitals and exclamation marks), and everything below describes that fallback. A negation reaches at most three words forward and never across a comma or full stop, so "No problems, great service" reads as positive. The answer names the words that carried the label, so it can be checked against the text, and names an emotional tone such as frustrated or joyful only when a word in the text states it and is not negated. A text with no opinion word is reported as neutral with that reason given. Sarcasm, irony and opinion words outside the list are not detected, so a neutral reading can be a miss. A hosted open-weight language model called over the network chooses among the supplied labels and explains the choice in a sentence or two; a label outside the supplied set is discarded. get.description: Example questions: "Summarise the evidence on intermittent fasting and weight loss". Returns answer, verdict, confidence, reason, checked_at and sources. PubMed and Europe PMC are searched on title and abstract, and from each study a single sentence reporting a result is quoted verbatim from its abstract and attributed by first author, year and PubMed id. A sentence is quoted only when it states a result, such as an association, a reduction or a conclusion, and when every topic word appears as a whole word in it or in the study's title.
